claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist as a homogeneous high-temperature BCC phase.
Al lowers the Gibbs free energy of BCC relative to competing phases in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The thermodynamic effect of Al is the primary cause of high-temperature BCC stability in this alloy.
Sluggish diffusion in the multicomponent matrix retards the atomic rearrangements required for phase transformation.
Without sufficient thermal activation, BCC is kinetically retained even where an FCC or ordered phase has lower equilibrium free energy.
Cooling rate and intermediate-temperature annealing duration govern phase selection in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Local chemical ordering induced by Al-dependent changes in the Gibbs free-energy landscape mediates the transition from disordered BCC to FCC or ordered secondary phases.
Additional atomic mobility supplied by slow cooling or annealing permits nucleation and growth of equilibrium FCC or ordered phases.
Rapid quenching from the high-temperature state will largely retain BCC.
Slow cooling or prolonged annealing near 700°C will increase the fraction of FCC or ordered secondary phases.
A rapidly cooled Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 specimen provides a uniform-BCC baseline.
Sluggish-diffusion limitations remain important below approximately 1000°C in this alloy.
Added elements or oxidation may alter the thermodynamic and kinetic balance governing phase stability.
The critical holding time and transformation temperature are uncertain because of variations in local diffusion and microstructural heterogeneity.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as a high-temperature BCC state, while the conditions call for processing at a high temperature described as 'above BCC stability.' If that phrase means outside the BCC stability range, the two statements conflict; the intended temperature relation is ambiguous.
